results.description: Response with special characters in text

guard_output.problem_summary: Type mismatch: cannot convert String to int.
guard_output.why: Java is strongly typed - you can't assign a String value to an int variable.
guard_output.hint_1: Look at the types on both sides of the '=' sign.
guard_output.learning_tip: Study Java's type system and casting rules.
guard_output.hint_2: Use Integer.parseInt() if you need to convert.

guard_output.problem_summary: The for loop has incorrect syntax using commas instead of semicolons.
guard_output.why: In Java, the three parts of a for loop header (initialization, condition, update) must be separated by semicolons, not commas. The compiler interprets commas differently and cannot parse the loop correctly.
guard_output.hint_1: Look at the separators between the three parts of your for loop header.
guard_output.learning_tip: Remember the for loop syntax: for(init; condition; update)
guard_output.hint_2: Replace the commas with semicolons in the for loop parentheses.

guard_output.problem_summary: ArithmeticException due to division by zero.
guard_output.why: Dividing an integer by zero is undefined in Java and throws an ArithmeticException at runtime.
guard_output.hint_1: Check the value of the divisor variable before the division.
guard_output.learning_tip: Always validate divisors to prevent ArithmeticException.
guard_output.hint_2: Add a condition to check if the divisor is zero before dividing.

guard_output.problem_summary: Variable not found - it was declared in a different scope.
guard_output.why: Variables declared inside an if block are only visible within that block. Once the block ends, the variable no longer exists.
guard_output.hint_1: Check where the variable 'result' is declared.
guard_output.learning_tip: Learn about variable scope and block-level declarations in Java.
guard_output.hint_2: Move the declaration outside the if block so it is accessible later.
guard_output.hint_3: Declare the variable before the if statement.

guard_output.why: Java method names are case-sensitive. The method 'lenght' does not exist on String.
guard_output.hint_1: Check the spelling of the method you are calling.
guard_output.learning_tip: Use IDE autocomplete to avoid typos in method names.
guard_output.hint_2: The correct method name uses standard English spelling.

guard_output.why: The recursive method never stops calling itself because there is no base case to terminate the recursion.
guard_output.hint_1: Look for a condition that should stop the recursion.
guard_output.learning_tip: Every recursive method needs a base case to prevent infinite recursion.
guard_output.hint_2: Add a base case that returns a value without making another recursive call.

guard_output.problem_summary: Cannot access a private field from outside the class.
guard_output.why: Private members are only accessible within the class that declares them. External code cannot read or modify them directly.
guard_output.hint_1: Check the access modifier of the field you are trying to use.
guard_output.learning_tip: Study Java access modifiers: public, private, protected, and default.
guard_output.hint_2: Use a public getter method to access the private field.

guard_output.problem_summary: Static context cannot reference non-static method.
guard_output.why: The main method is static but display() is not. Static methods cannot call instance methods directly.
guard_output.hint_1: You need an object instance to call a non-static method.
guard_output.learning_tip: Understand the difference between static and instance members.

guard_output.problem_summary: ClassCastException when casting String to Integer.
guard_output.why: Even though both are Objects, a String cannot be cast to Integer because they are unrelated types in the class hierarchy.
guard_output.hint_1: Check what type the object actually is before casting.
guard_output.learning_tip: Learn about Java type hierarchy and safe casting with instanceof.
guard_output.hint_2: Use instanceof to verify the type before attempting a cast.

guard_output.problem_summary: Array created with negative size throws NegativeArraySizeException.
guard_output.why: Java does not allow arrays with negative length. The size must be >= 0.
guard_output.hint_1: Check the value passed to new int[...] - it must not be negative.
guard_output.learning_tip: Validate array sizes before allocation to avoid runtime exceptions.
guard_output.hint_2: Ensure the size variable is 0 or greater before creating the array.

guard_output.problem_summary: NumberFormatException when parsing a non-numeric string.
guard_output.why: Integer.parseInt() expects a string containing only digits. Letters or special characters cause this exception.
guard_output.hint_1: Check what string value you are passing to parseInt().
guard_output.learning_tip: Use try-catch or regex validation before parsing strings to numbers.
guard_output.hint_2: Validate the string contains only digits before parsing.
